title: Twelve Long-Hidden Paintings Head to Auction
summary: Their pre-sale estimates total about $450 million.

1.content:
Twelve paintings from a private collection will sell at Sotheby's in New York on November 18. The paintings include works by Vincent van Gogh, Claude Monet, and Paul Cézanne. It is the pre-sale estimate for all twelve paintings: about $450 million.

Some of the paintings have not been shown publicly for more than 50 years. One Van Gogh painting, Châtaigniers en fleurs, has an estimate of about $180 million. An estimate is the price an auction house thinks a work may sell for. It is not the final sale price. Famous paintings do not always hang in museums. A family or private collector can keep a painting at home, in storage, or lend it to a museum.

vocabulary.definition: owned by a person or family, not by the public
a careful guess about a future price or amount
a sale where buyers offer prices for something

quiz.question: What does the $450 million figure mean?
options: It is the price of one painting by Claude Monet.
It is the final sale price for all twelve paintings.
It is the pre-sale estimate for all twelve paintings: about $450 million.

2.content:
On November 18, Sotheby's will auction twelve paintings in New York from the Blaquier-Arrieta collection. The group includes work by Van Gogh, Cézanne, Monet, and other artists. Sotheby's says the collection has pre-sale estimates of about $450 million.

The largest estimate is about $180 million for Van Gogh's Châtaigniers en fleurs. Cézanne's Arlequin has an estimate around $120 million. An auction estimate is not a promise; the final price depends on what buyers offer during the sale.

The paintings belonged to a private collection and were mostly bought in London in the 1970s. Some were kept in a private collection and not shown publicly for 50 years or more. A private owner can keep art at home, store it, lend it to a museum, or show it only rarely.

That is why a famous painting can disappear from public view without being lost. The auction will bring these works back before the public, but it does not mean a museum will buy them. The winning buyers will decide where the paintings go next.

vocabulary.definition: a sale in which people compete by offering prices
an expected price, not a guaranteed result
belonging to an individual or family rather than the public
in a way that people can see or know about

quiz.question: What does an auction estimate tell buyers?
options: The auction house has already sold every painting.
An auction estimate is not a promise; the final price depends on what buyers offer during the sale.
A museum must buy the paintings after the sale.

quiz.question: Why had some paintings not been publicly shown for decades?
options: Some were kept in a private collection and not shown publicly for 50 years or more.
No one knew that Van Gogh and Monet were artists.

3.content:
An important private collection will be sold at Sotheby's in New York on November 18. It contains twelve Impressionist and modern paintings, including works by Vincent van Gogh, Paul Cézanne, and Claude Monet. Sotheby's places the combined pre-sale estimates at about $450 million.

The leading lot is Van Gogh's Châtaigniers en fleurs, estimated at about $180 million. It was painted in May 1890, after Van Gogh arrived in Auvers-sur-Oise. Cézanne's Arlequin is estimated around $120 million. Sotheby's says the two paintings could set auction records, but that is a prediction, not a result.

The paintings were collected in the 1970s by Carlos Pedro Blaquier and Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier. Some of the works have not been seen on public exhibition for 50 years or longer. Reuters reported that five paintings were shown at Sotheby's in London, while the rest were being shown digitally before selected works travel to galleries worldwide.

A private collection is art owned by an individual or family rather than a museum. Private owners may store a painting, show it at home, lend it to an exhibition, or keep it away from public view. This auction will make the collection easier to see, but the estimated $450 million is still not its final sale price.

vocabulary.definition: a group of objects gathered and owned by one person or organization
judged to have an approximate value
a sale where the highest offer usually wins
a public show of art or other objects
a statement about what may happen in the future

quiz.question: What does Sotheby's say about the collection's $450 million figure?
options: Sotheby's places the combined pre-sale estimates at about $450 million.
It is the final amount already paid by museums.
It is the cost of shipping the paintings around the world.

quiz.question: What is a private collection?
options: A private collection is a public room that shows every artwork for free.
A private collection is art owned by an individual or family rather than a museum.
A private collection is a list of paintings made by one artist.

quiz.question: What is still uncertain about the two leading paintings?
options: The two paintings have never been seen by any person.
The two paintings were made by artists no one can identify.
Sotheby's says the two paintings could set auction records, but that is a prediction, not a result.

title: Momenta Plans Robotaxi Tests in More Cities
summary: It aims to expand from trials in China, Munich, and Abu Dhabi.

1.content:
Momenta is a Chinese company that makes robotaxis. A robotaxi is a car that can drive itself. The company is testing these cars in five Chinese cities, Munich in Germany, and Abu Dhabi in the UAE.

Momenta wants to send robotaxis to Dubai next year. It is also talking with more European cities, and Japan is a priority. The company has more than 100 robotaxis in three countries. It hopes to have hundreds of cars by the end of 2026 and several thousand by the end of 2027.

A self-driving car needs tests in every new place. Roads, traffic, and local rules can be different. Testing helps the company learn whether the car can drive safely in that city.

vocabulary.definition: a taxi that can drive itself
trying something carefully to see how it works
in a way that avoids danger

quiz.question: Why does a self-driving car need tests in a new place?
options: Roads, traffic, and local rules can be different.
It can use the same rules in every city without checking.
It must stop driving as soon as it leaves China.

2.content:
Momenta Global is a Chinese self-driving company. It has more than 100 robotaxis in three countries, although its robotaxi business is still at an early stage. It is testing in five Chinese cities, Munich, and Abu Dhabi.

According to a Momenta executive, the company plans to deploy vehicles in Dubai next year. It is talking with a few European cities about further expansion, and Japan is also a priority market. The company hopes its fleet will reach hundreds by the end of 2026 and several thousand by the end of 2027.

A robotaxi is not simply a normal car without a driver. It has to observe roads, other vehicles, people, and local traffic rules. A new city can have different road designs, weather, driving patterns, and legal requirements. Testing in one city does not automatically prove that a service can work in another city.

That is why trials matter. They allow a company to test how its system works in a new local environment before a wider service begins.

vocabulary.definition: growth into more places or activities
a group of vehicles owned or operated together
to watch carefully and notice information
rules or conditions that must be met

quiz.question: Where is Momenta testing robotaxis now?
options: It is testing in five Chinese cities, Munich, and Abu Dhabi.
It is testing only in Tokyo and Dubai.
It has stopped all testing outside China.

quiz.question: Why do trials in a new city matter?
options: They remove the need to follow local rules.
They allow a company to test how its system works in a new local environment before a wider service begins.
They prove that every city has identical traffic.

3.content:
Chinese autonomous-driving company Momenta is planning a wider robotaxi expansion. Reuters reported that Momenta has more than 100 robotaxis in three countries. Momenta is testing robotaxis in five Chinese cities, Munich, and Abu Dhabi.

The company says it plans to deploy vehicles in Dubai next year and is talking with a few European cities. Japan is another priority. Shuo Xie, who leads Momenta's robotaxi business, said the fleet should be in the hundreds by the end of 2026 and reach several thousand by the end of 2027. These are company goals, not a guarantee.

The story is also about the difficulty of entering a new city. A self-driving system must deal with local road layouts, traffic signs, other road users, weather, and rules. A city may also set its own conditions for testing and commercial service. A successful trial in one location does not mean the technology has already been proven everywhere.

Momenta's trials in Munich and Abu Dhabi are therefore important steps, but they are not the same as a broad public launch. Testing helps a company see how its system performs in a particular local environment before it expands. For riders, the key question is not only whether a car can drive, but whether it can drive safely in their city.

vocabulary.definition: able to operate without a human controlling every action
to send or put something into use
rules or situations that affect what can happen
connected with providing a service for payment
works or does a task in a particular way

quiz.question: Where is Momenta already testing robotaxis?
options: Momenta is testing robotaxis in five Chinese cities, Munich, and Abu Dhabi.

quiz.question: How should readers understand Momenta's fleet targets?
options: They are final numbers already reached by the company.
They are rules set by every city in Europe.
These are company goals, not a guarantee.

quiz.question: What can testing help a company learn?
options: Testing removes all weather and traffic differences.
Testing helps a company see how its system performs in a particular local environment before it expands.
Testing means a public service has already launched everywhere.

title: One Shark Draws 600,000 Busan Visitors
summary: Officials are trying to guide it back to sea.

1.content:
A very large shark has become famous in Busan, South Korea. The shark was first seen in a narrow canal at North Port on September 18. It is about 3.5 metres long and has stayed there for many days.

People call the shark Bukangi. About 600,000 people came to see it in less than two weeks, city officials said. During the Chuseok holiday, about 480,000 visitors went to the park near the canal. Usually, the park has about 2,000 visitors on a weekend day. Officials want the shark to return to the sea. They tried to guide it out with water from boats, but it swam away. The rescue is for a wild animal, not a pet or show animal.

vocabulary.definition: a narrow waterway made or used by people
people who go to see a place or event
an effort to save a person or animal from danger

quiz.question: Why are officials planning another rescue effort?
options: Officials want the shark to return to the sea.
They want the shark to attract more visitors forever.
They want to make the shark a pet in the park.

2.content:
A shark known as Bukangi has become an unusual attraction in Busan, South Korea. It was spotted on September 18 in a narrow canal at North Port. It is about 3.5 metres long and has remained in the waterway instead of returning to open water.

The city counted about 600,000 visitors from September 19. About 480,000 came during the four-day Chuseok holiday. Busan later named Bukangi an honorary public relations ambassador after about 8,200 people joined an online poll and 91% supported the idea.

News reports describe the shark as a bronze whaler, but its species has been reported differently in early coverage. The nickname joins Buk Hang, the Korean name for North Port, with the Korean ending -i.

Authorities do not see the canal as a permanent home. A first effort used boats to spray water behind it, hoping to guide it toward the sea. The shark avoided the water streams. Officials said a future effort may use a large net to channel it toward the exit. Their goal is to return the wild animal safely to open water.

vocabulary.definition: something that brings people to a place
a person or symbol chosen to represent a place or group
to guide movement in a particular direction
intended to last for a long time

quiz.question: How did Busan give Bukangi a city role?
options: Busan moved Bukangi into a city aquarium.
Busan gave Bukangi a job as a park safety officer.
Busan later named Bukangi an honorary public relations ambassador after about 8,200 people joined an online poll and 91% supported the idea.

quiz.question: What happened during the first effort to guide the shark out?
options: The shark was moved into a permanent tank.
The shark avoided the water streams.
The shark reached the sea after one minute.

3.content:
A 3.5-metre shark, nicknamed Bukangi, has remained in a narrow canal at Busan's North Port since it was first spotted on September 18. Busan said about 600,000 people had visited the site by Sept 28, including 480,000 during the Chuseok holiday.

Busan used that public interest in an online poll. About 8,200 people took part, and 91% supported making Bukangi an honorary public relations ambassador. This is a symbolic city role, not a change in the shark's legal or biological status. The name combines Buk Hang, or North Port, with the familiar Korean ending -i.

Authorities are focused on releasing the shark, not keeping it in the canal. A first operation deployed boats that sprayed water behind it, aiming to guide it toward open sea. The shark avoided the streams, and the operation was stopped. Officials then said they were considering a specially designed net, stretched across the waterway, to channel the shark toward the exit.

Reports have called the animal a bronze whaler shark, but species identification varied in early coverage. Officials have not reported clear signs that its health has worsened, yet they say release is important for its safety and long-term health. The crowds are part of the story, but the rescue objective remains to return a wild animal to open water as safely as possible.

connected with living things
sent or put into use
the process of deciding what something is
the goal someone is trying to achieve

quiz.question: What did the honorary ambassador title change?
options: It ended the need for a rescue operation.
It made the shark a permanent resident of the canal.
This is a symbolic city role, not a change in the shark's legal or biological status.

quiz.question: Why do officials still want to release the shark?
options: They say release is important for its safety and long-term health.
The crowds stopped visiting the canal.
They want to turn the canal into an aquarium.

title: Cockpit Attack Forces Flight to Make Emergency Landing
summary: All 174 passengers reached safety after the diversion.

1.content:
A flydubai plane was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. During the flight, there was a serious incident in the cockpit, where the pilots sit. The plane made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

The airline said there was an altercation, or a serious fight, in the cockpit. The crew secured the plane and landed it safely. All 174 passengers and the crew were reported safe. The captain and first officer were hurt and taken to hospital. The plane sent emergency signals during the event. Saudi officials are investigating what happened. The reason for the fight has not been officially established. A second plane later took the passengers to Tel Aviv.

vocabulary.definition: the part of an aircraft where pilots control the flight
a serious argument or fight
trying to find the facts about an event

quiz.question: What is known about the reason for the cockpit fight?
options: Saudi officials have already officially established the reason.
The reason for the fight has not been officially established.
The reason was announced by the airline before the plane landed.

2.content:
Flydubai flight FZ1073 left Dubai for Tel Aviv on September 30 with 174 passengers. It later diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia after a serious cockpit incident. Flydubai said an altercation occurred in the flight deck and that crew members secured the aircraft.

Flight-tracking data showed a sharp descent during the emergency. The aircraft went from about 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet in about one minute, according to Flightradar24 data reported by the Associated Press. It then reached Tabuk safely.

The plane first transmitted 7700, an international code for a general emergency. It later sent 7500, which signals unlawful interference with an aircraft and can include a possible hijacking. These codes show controllers that an aircraft needs urgent attention; they do not, by themselves, explain the cause.

Saudi Arabia's safety center has opened an investigation. The airport said the captain and first officer were injured and went to hospital. The airline arranged another flight for passengers. Officials have not established a motive, and reports about an attempted crash remain unconfirmed.

vocabulary.definition: sent to a different place from the planned destination
sent a signal or message electronically
an action that wrongly affects or interrupts something
a reason for doing something

quiz.question: What did the 7500 code signal?
options: It signalled a routine request for more fuel.
It signalled that the flight had reached its planned destination.
It later sent 7500, which signals unlawful interference with an aircraft and can include a possible hijacking.

quiz.question: What does the Level 2 reading say about the emergency codes?
options: These codes are only used after all passengers leave a plane.
These codes show controllers that an aircraft needs urgent attention; they do not, by themselves, explain the cause.
These codes prove that a hijacking happened.

3.content:
Flydubai flight FZ1073, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, on September 30 after a cockpit emergency. Flydubai confirmed that an altercation occurred in the flight deck and said crew members secured the aircraft, diverted it and landed safely. Saudi Arabia's National Transport Safety Center has opened an investigation.

Associated Press reporting, citing Flightradar24 data, said the Boeing 737 Max 8 descended from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet in about a minute. The aircraft transmitted 7700, the general emergency code, and then 7500, which indicates unlawful interference. These transponder signals alert air traffic control but do not establish why an emergency happened.

The airport said the captain and first officer were injured and taken to hospital. All 174 passengers and crew were safe, and a replacement aircraft continued the journey. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said one pilot stabbed the other and apparently tried to crash the aircraft. However, Flydubai did not publicly identify a motive, and independent confirmation of a crash or hijacking attempt was not available.

This distinction matters in early reporting. An investigation needs physical evidence, cockpit information, crew accounts and flight data before it can determine what happened and why. Until then, the confirmed facts are the cockpit incident, emergency signals, diversion and safe landing—not a final explanation of intent.

vocabulary.definition: an aircraft device that sends identification and status signals
shows that something may be true
proof that something is true
real and able to be seen or touched
what someone planned or meant to do

quiz.question: Which details did flydubai confirm publicly?
options: The first officer's motive for the incident.
Flydubai confirmed that an altercation occurred in the flight deck and said crew members secured the aircraft, diverted it and landed safely.
That a hijacking attempt had been independently confirmed.

quiz.question: What can the transponder signals tell air traffic control?
options: These transponder signals alert air traffic control but do not establish why an emergency happened.
They identify the motive of everyone in the cockpit.
They prove a final explanation of intent.

quiz.question: Why should reporting avoid a final explanation of intent now?
options: The safe landing means investigators need no evidence.
Emergency codes always provide a complete explanation by themselves.
An investigation needs physical evidence, cockpit information, crew accounts and flight data before it can determine what happened and why.

title: Vermont Homes Form a Virtual Power Plant
summary: Their batteries help during outages and busy hours.

1.content:
Thousands of homes in Vermont have batteries. These batteries can keep lights on when a storm cuts the power. But they can also work together.

The local power company, Green Mountain Power, can use some stored energy when many people need electricity. This group of home batteries is called a virtual power plant. It is not one big building. It is many small batteries linked by software. The company says more than 5,000 customers are now part of the system. Before a possible storm, the company keeps power in the batteries for the homes. At busy times, the shared energy can reduce pressure on the electricity grid. This may lower costs and reduce the need for polluting power plants.

vocabulary.definition: devices that store electricity for later use
connected by technology instead of being in one real place
the network that carries electricity to homes and businesses

quiz.question: What happens before a possible storm?
options: The company keeps power in the batteries for the homes.
The grid stops carrying electricity to every customer.
The company removes all batteries from homes.

2.content:
A power plant is usually one large place that makes electricity. In Vermont, Green Mountain Power is building a different kind of resource. It links stored energy in thousands of homes, batteries, and devices. Together, they form a virtual power plant, or VPP.

The system does not create electricity by itself. Instead, software coordinates energy that is already stored. During times of peak demand, when electricity use is very high, the company can draw on part of that energy. Customers still keep reserve power, especially when bad weather could cause outages.

As of July 2026, GMP said its VPP could provide 110 megawatts of power. More than half came from home energy-storage systems. The company said its network sent 90 megawatts of stored energy during a July heat event and saved customers about $6 million in one peak hour.

GMP says the growing system has helped it permanently close two fossil-fuel peaker plants. The VPP may make the grid cleaner and cheaper, but it still depends on customers joining, usable batteries, and careful grid management.

vocabulary.definition: organizes different parts so they work together
the highest point or time of use
a supply kept for a future need
using coal, oil, or natural gas for energy

quiz.question: What does a virtual power plant do with the energy in this story?
options: It creates electricity by itself from nothing.
It sends all home batteries away during storms.
Instead, software coordinates energy that is already stored.

quiz.question: What did GMP say its network did during the July heat event?
options: The company said its network sent 90 megawatts of stored energy during a July heat event and saved customers about $6 million in one peak hour.
The company said it built two new fossil-fuel peaker plants.
The company said it stopped every Vermont power outage forever.

3.content:
Green Mountain Power is expanding a virtual power plant built from distributed energy resources. Its network combines home batteries, utility-scale batteries, electric-vehicle chargers, flexible commercial buildings, and hydropower. Software coordinates them when the grid needs help.

GMP said that, as of July 2026, more than 5,000 customers had more than 10,000 batteries in its programmes. The VPP had 110MW of capacity, with more than half coming from residential storage. This figure measures how much power the system can deliver, not a claim that the VPP produces electricity like a conventional generator.

During a July heat event, GMP said it deployed 90MW of carbon-free stored energy and saved an estimated $6 million in one peak hour. The company says its storage network has allowed it to permanently close two peaker plants, which are usually used only at high-demand times. Those fossil-fuel plants can be expensive and polluting.

For households, the same batteries can offer backup during outages. GMP says it takes steps to preserve home backup when weather is forecast to cause outages. The model still has limits: its benefits depend on enough customers enrolling, equipment working, software coordination, and rules that let utilities use distributed resources. It is a way to manage existing energy more flexibly, not a complete replacement for every part of the power system.

vocabulary.definition: spread across many places instead of kept in one place
the maximum amount a system can provide
following the usual traditional method
put into use for a particular purpose
in a way that can change for different needs

quiz.question: Which resources does GMP combine in its virtual power plant?
options: Its network combines home batteries, utility-scale batteries, electric-vehicle chargers, flexible commercial buildings, and hydropower.
Only power lines with no stored energy.

quiz.question: What does the 110MW figure describe?
options: This figure measures how much power the system can deliver, not a claim that the VPP produces electricity like a conventional generator.
It is the number of households that lost power in July.
It proves the VPP creates all electricity used in Vermont.

quiz.question: What limitation does the Level 3 reading give for this model?
options: It works only when no batteries are connected.
It can replace every part of the power system immediately.
Its benefits depend on enough customers enrolling, equipment working, software coordination, and rules that let utilities use distributed resources.

title: Cat Cancer Study May Benefit Pets and People
summary: Nearly 500 tumors reveal shared genetic clues across species.

1.content:
Scientists studied cancer samples from almost 500 pet cats in five countries. They looked for genetic changes that help tumors grow. Many of the same cancer-related genes are also found in people and dogs.

One example is a gene called FBXW7. More than half of the cat breast tumors in the study had a change in this gene. A similar change is linked with human breast cancer.

The team also tested some medicines on cat tumor tissue. Certain drugs worked better on samples with the gene change. But this was a test on tissue, not on living cats. Researchers hope the findings will help veterinarians improve care for cats and may give human cancer research useful clues too.

vocabulary.definition: Connected with genes, the instructions found in living cells.
A mass of cells that grow in an uncontrolled way.
A group of cells from a living body.

quiz.question: What did the researchers test some medicines on?

2.content:
An international team analyzed cancer tissue from almost 500 domestic cats in five countries. The scientists searched for genetic changes that help tumors begin and grow. They found that many cancer-driving genes in cats are also known in human and dog cancers.

One example came from mammary tumors, which grow in breast tissue. The most common driver gene in the cat tumors was FBXW7. More than half of the samples had a mutation in that gene. In people, a similar mutation in breast cancer is linked with a worse outlook.

The team also tested chemotherapy drugs on tumor samples. Some drugs worked better on cat mammary tissue with the FBXW7 mutation. This result came from tissue tests only; it does not show that the drugs will work in living cats or people.

Cats may still offer useful clues because they naturally develop cancer and often share homes and environmental exposures with people. The study could support more personalized treatment for pets and point scientists toward questions about human cancer. Any treatment benefit for either species will need further study.

vocabulary.definition: A change in the DNA instructions inside a cell.
Related to the breast or milk-producing glands.
Contact with something in the environment, such as smoke or chemicals.
Chosen for the needs or features of one particular person or case.

quiz.question: What did the study find about many cat cancer genes?
options: They prove that all cancers have the same cause
also known in human and dog cancers

quiz.question: What is the limit of the drug result reported here?
options: does not show that the drugs will work in living cats or people
It showed that no drugs affected the samples
It proved a cure in living cats

3.content:
An international study mapped genetic changes in cancers from almost 500 domestic cats across five countries. Researchers found that many genes that drive feline tumors are also involved in cancers in people and dogs. The findings may help veterinary medicine and human cancer research, though they do not establish a ready-made treatment.

The clearest example involved mammary, or breast, tumors. FBXW7 was the most common driver gene in the cat mammary samples, and more than half carried a mutation in it. In people, mutations in FBXW7 are associated with a worse prognosis in breast cancer. Similarities appeared in several other cancer types too.

Scientists tested chemotherapy drugs on cat tumor tissue. Some drugs were more effective in samples with the mutated FBXW7 gene. However, this result came from tissue in a laboratory; it does not show that the drugs will work in living cats or humans. Clinical research would be needed to answer that question.

Cats naturally develop cancer and often share environments with people, so they may help researchers explore how genes and surroundings interact. The study also created a genetic resource for future work. In a two-way approach sometimes called One Medicine, knowledge from veterinary studies could inform human research, while treatments developed for people might eventually be evaluated for pets. Both possibilities remain areas for further study.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to cats.
A medical judgment about how an illness may develop.
Able to produce the result that is wanted.
To affect or influence one another.
Carefully studied or judged to understand quality or effect.

quiz.question: What did the study establish about chemotherapy drugs?
options: They are already approved for all cats with cancer
Some drugs were more effective in samples with the mutated FBXW7 gene
They cure breast cancer in people

quiz.question: Why might cats be useful in cancer research?
options: They have exactly the same cancers as humans
They do not need clinical research
Cats naturally develop cancer and often share environments with people

quiz.question: What does the two-way One Medicine approach mean?
options: Only human treatments can help animals
Animal studies replace all human cancer research
knowledge from veterinary studies could inform human research

title: Milky Way’s First Microblazar Aims a Jet Toward Earth
summary: The distant system may accelerate extremely energetic particles.

1.content:
Astronomers have identified the first known microblazar in the Milky Way. It is a binary system: a black hole and a massive star orbit each other. The black hole pulls gas from the star. Some gas forms a hot disk, while some shoots out in narrow jets.

One jet points almost along our line of sight. This direction makes the system look unusually bright, but it does not mean Earth is in danger.

Radio images also show the jet hitting a cloud of gas and dust. Scientists think this area may speed up tiny particles to nearly the speed of light. They are studying the system to learn how such powerful particles form.

vocabulary.definition: Made of two parts or objects that are linked.
Narrow, fast streams of matter or energy sent out into space.
Very small pieces of matter.

quiz.question: Why does the microblazar look unusually bright?
options: One jet points almost along our line of sight
The star has stopped orbiting the black hole
The system is inside Earth’s atmosphere

2.content:
The first known Milky Way microblazar, IRAS 18293−0941, is a black hole and a massive star orbiting every 11 days. The black hole pulls gas from the star into a hot, spinning disk. Some gas is then fired into space in narrow jets from its poles.

One jet points very close to Earth’s line of sight. Fast-moving radiation aimed toward us can appear brighter, like a flashlight pointed toward your eyes. This effect helps explain why distant blazars look so bright. The alignment is not a danger to Earth.

Radio images show the jet crossing about 100 light-years of space before hitting a dense cloud of gas and dust. At a bright spot there, the jet may accelerate particles to nearly the speed of light and very high energies. The spot also matches a gamma-ray signal.

Researchers describe the system as a potential particle accelerator. More observations will test how the jet heats the cloud and whether it links to the nearby high-energy source.

vocabulary.definition: Turning around a central point.
Energy that travels through space as waves or particles.
Having many things packed closely together.
Possible or able to happen, but not yet certain.

quiz.question: How does the black hole get material for its disk and jets?
options: It takes matter from Earth’s atmosphere
It collects water from the molecular cloud
The black hole pulls gas from the star into a hot, spinning disk

quiz.question: What did the radio images reveal before the jet reaches the cloud?
options: The jet had already left the Milky Way
the jet crossing about 100 light-years of space before hitting a dense cloud of gas and dust
The jet stopped moving near the star

3.content:
A newly identified Milky Way microblazar lets astronomers study blazars normally seen around supermassive black holes in distant galaxies. The object, IRAS 18293−0941, is a binary system: a black hole about ten times the Sun’s mass and a massive star orbiting one another roughly every 11 days. Gas pulled from the star forms a disk; some then escapes as narrow jets from the black hole’s poles.

One jet is aligned very close to our line of sight. Because its material moves at relativistic speeds, radiation directed toward Earth can appear unusually bright. This beaming effect is one reason blazars are so luminous. The alignment is an observing geometry, not evidence that Earth is threatened.

Radio observations trace the jet across roughly 100 light-years before it meets a dense molecular cloud. The impact region is bright, and researchers report that it coincides with a gamma-ray signature. title: Indri Lemurs Use a Soprano-Like Singing Trick
summary: Wider mouths may help their high notes travel farther.

1.content:
Indris are lemurs that live in the rainforests of Madagascar. They are the only lemurs known for singing. In a thick forest, trees and leaves can block what an animal can see. So an indri's song helps family groups communicate.

Scientists found something special about these songs. When an indri sings a higher note, it opens its mouth wider. A wider mouth changes the shape of the mouth and throat. This can help the sound travel farther.

A new study found that indris open their mouths wider for higher notes. Researchers looked at 83 videos of 19 wild indris. They compared the animals' mouth movements with the pitch of their songs. The link between wider mouths and higher pitch was strong.

This pattern is consistent with formant tuning. The mouth and throat act a little like a tube. When their shape changes, the sound can resonate differently. A better match between the voice and the vocal tract may make a high note more powerful and help it travel farther.

Trained opera singers use a similar technique. The finding does not mean an indri is an opera singer. It shows that animals and humans can use similar body changes when they face a similar sound problem: how to make a high note carry through a large space.

As pitch rose, mouth opening increased. The pattern was robust and is consistent with formant tuning, a technique associated with trained singers.

Formants are resonance frequencies shaped by the vocal tract: the mouth and throat. When an indri opens its mouth wider on a high note, it changes that tube-like space. This can bring a resonance closer to the sound being produced, which can increase vocal power and help a call carry farther. The study describes a link between mouth opening and pitch; it does not mean that every indri song works exactly like a human performance.

The comparison is useful because both species face a physical problem: how to be heard at a distance. Human and lemur lineages split roughly 70 million years ago, Reuters reported. title: Antarctic Ozone Layer Shows Signs of Recovery

The ozone layer is high above Earth. It helps protect people, animals, and plants from harmful ultraviolet light from the sun. But in the 1980s, scientists saw a large ozone hole over Antarctica each spring.

Susan Solomon, an American scientist, helped explain the problem. Some chemicals called CFCs could stay in the air for many years. High in the atmosphere, they released chlorine. This chlorine damaged ozone. In 1987, many countries made the Montreal Protocol. They agreed to stop using more of these chemicals. Solomon says the ozone layer is now showing recovery. At a lecture in Taipei on Sept. 19, 2026, atmospheric scientist Susan Solomon described the Antarctic ozone layer as a major success for science and international policy. Her work helped explain why a dramatic ozone decline appeared over Antarctica in the early 1980s.

CFCs were used in products such as refrigerators, air conditioners, and spray cans. They can remain in the atmosphere for decades. Sunlight can break them down and release chlorine atoms. The atoms can take part in reactions that destroy ozone again and again.

Solomon found that Antarctica's extreme cold creates polar stratospheric clouds. Their surfaces help activate chlorine. When sunlight returns in spring, ozone destruction speeds up. Scientists' evidence helped lead to the 1987 Montreal Protocol.

The treaty later reached 197 United Nations member states and reduced CFC concentrations. Measurements show the ozone hole is forming more slowly. Still, recovery will take decades, and wildfire smoke or CFC leakage could slow it.

Solomon later showed that very cold polar stratospheric clouds provide surfaces for reactions that activate chlorine. When spring sunlight returns, those reactions accelerate ozone destruction.

Evidence from several research groups helped prompt the Montreal Protocol in 1987. It progressively controlled ozone-depleting substances and gave financial assistance to developing countries adopting alternatives. Solomon said the agreement had been signed by 197 United Nations member states. Atmospheric CFC concentrations have fallen, and the ozone hole now forms more slowly than it did when chlorine levels peaked.

This progress has limits. CFCs have long atmospheric lifetimes, so full recovery will take decades. The story shows that international cooperation can work, but monitoring and practical solutions still matter.

title: Ancient Clay Beads Hold Children’s Fingerprints
summary: Natufian ornaments reveal makers from 15,000 years ago.

1.content:
Archaeologists studied tiny clay ornaments made up to 15,000 years ago. The objects came from Natufian sites in what is now Israel. They were made before farming and pottery became common in the region.

The small beads and pendants still hold fingerprints from the people who shaped them. Researchers found about 50 prints from adults, children and teenagers.

The ornaments were made from clay and shaped into small discs, rings and other forms. Some looked like plants. A child's fingerprint makes the past feel close: long ago, young people were learning to make things with their hands, too, in daily life.

the unique lines left by the skin of a finger

2.content:
A fingerprint can turn an ancient object into a human story. Researchers studied 142 small clay beads and pendants from Natufian sites in what is now Israel. The ornaments are between about 11,650 and 15,000 years old.

The Natufian people were hunter-gatherers living before agriculture and pottery became widespread in the region. Yet they already used clay to make personal ornaments. The pieces included discs, rings, cylinders and bead shapes that copied plants such as barley, wheat, lentils and peas. Some were colored with red ochre.

Researchers identified about 50 fingerprints. By comparing the width of the fingerprint ridges with a modern experimental dataset, they estimated that adults, children and teenagers worked with the clay. Five ornaments had prints linked to children or younger people.

This does not show exactly what each child was taught or why every ornament was made. But it offers direct evidence that young people were makers, not only watchers. The study suggests that making ornaments may have been a shared activity where skills and social values passed between generations.

3.content:
Small clay ornaments from the Natufian culture have preserved an unusually personal kind of evidence: the makers' fingerprints. A study examined 142 beads and pendants from Israel, dating from about 15,000 to 11,650 years ago. The objects were made before agriculture and pottery became widespread.

The ornaments included discs, rings, cylinders and forms that resemble plants, including barley, wheat, lentils and peas. Some carried a red ochre coating. Their surfaces also retained fingerprints and palm prints from the people who pressed, pinched and shaped wet clay.

Researchers measured the mean ridge breadth of about 50 prints against modern data. Their analysis identified makers from different age groups. Five of the six ornaments carrying fingerprints were attributed to children or subadults; the other was linked to a young adult or adult female. Clay can shrink as it dries, so the study treats these age estimates carefully, not as exact identities.

The finding does not let archaeologists reconstruct one family's day. It does, however, provide direct evidence that children participated in making personal ornaments. That matters because the objects were part of shared symbolic practices in early settled communities. A small fingerprint does not answer every question about the past, but it connects an abstract culture with a person who once pressed a finger into soft clay.

title: Why Do World Leaders Meet at the UN?

1.content:
This week, world leaders are meeting in New York at the United Nations. About 130 presidents and prime ministers will come. They will speak about problems.

The meeting is called the General Debate. Leaders talk about wars, climate change, trade and new technology such as AI. The United Nations has 193 member countries. Each country can have a voice there.

The UN cannot make every country do what it wants. Countries often disagree. But the meeting is useful. Leaders can talk in smaller meetings, too. They may discuss peace, food, trade or help for people in danger. Talking does not always bring an agreement. But it can be harder to solve a problem when countries do not talk at all.

Nearly 130 heads of state and government are expected in New York for the United Nations General Assembly's High-level Week. The General Debate runs from September 22 to 28. Leaders explain priorities to a global audience.

The UN has 193 member states, and each one has a vote in the General Assembly. That gives small countries a chance to speak with large powers. Leaders are expected to discuss wars, climate action, trade and artificial intelligence. These problems cross borders, so one country cannot always manage them alone.

Still, the UN is not a world government. The General Assembly can make recommendations, but it usually cannot force countries to follow them. The Security Council has stronger power over peace and security. Its five permanent members can use a veto to block a decision.

The speeches are only part of the week. Leaders and diplomats also hold bilateral meetings, meaning meetings between two countries. They may disagree in public but still need to discuss aid, security or trade. A meeting cannot promise peace. It can keep communication open when agreement is difficult.

The agenda is broad because the problems are connected. Wars, climate change, trade disruption, pandemics and artificial intelligence can affect people beyond one border. The General Assembly gives all 193 member states one vote, so a small island state can speak on the same stage as a major power. Its resolutions usually express collective views or recommendations rather than laws that countries must obey.

This structure explains a common frustration. The UN cannot act like a world government and order countries to end a war. The Security Council can make stronger decisions, but a negative vote from any of its five permanent members can block a decision. When powerful countries have conflicting interests, a shared response can be hard.

Yet the speeches are only one purpose of the gathering. Ministers and diplomats schedule bilateral conversations between two governments. They can raise humanitarian aid, trade, prisoners or ways to prevent a crisis from growing. These talks may not create an immediate agreement, but they create contact. In a divided world, that diplomatic space remains valuable: many problems cannot be managed by one country alone.

Three African wild dog brothers left their home in Zambia and travelled an amazing 4,126 kilometers. Their trip lasted about nine months. Scientists say it is the longest recorded journey by a land mammal in Africa.

African wild dogs live in social family groups called packs. When young adults leave their birth pack to find unrelated animals and a new territory, scientists call it dispersal. Researchers used GPS collars to track the brothers as they crossed protected and unprotected land.

The dogs moved toward the cities of Kitwe and Ndola, then changed direction rather than entering the busiest areas. By April 2026, they had settled in the Luano Game Management Area in the Luangwa Valley ecosystem. title: Burkina Faso’s Deaf Dancers Feel Music Through Vibrations

1.content:
Fientan Company is a dance group in Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso. Its dancers are deaf or hard of hearing. Yet they perform together to drums and djembes. They use a technique called Vibra-Signe to keep time without depending only on sound.

Choreographer Yaya Sanou created the method. Dancers use sign language, visual gestures, physical touch, and vibrations. When they dance barefoot, vibrations from the music can travel through the ground. Sanou may tap a dancer’s body to help them feel the musical tempo.

Vibra-Signe lets dancers connect music, movement, and signs. It gives them ways to communicate and share their stories. The group shows that people can experience rhythm through their bodies, not only through their ears.

2.content:
Fientan Company, based in Bobo-Dioulasso in Burkina Faso, brings together deaf and hard-of-hearing dancers. Founded in 2018 by choreographer Yaya Sanou, it uses Vibra-Signe, a technique that helps dancers follow music through more than hearing.

The technique mixes sign language, visual gestures, expression, physical touch, and body vibrations. During barefoot dance, vibrations rise from the floor. Sanou can tap dancers’ bodies to help them catch the tempo. He says sight helps performers see and carry out movements, while signs can sign the dance.

Exercise is important. Experts say that aerobic fitness, flexibility and muscle strength can help people remain mobile and independent later in life. Activities such as walking, cycling, tennis and badminton can add movement. Even a brisk 15-minute walk after a meal can be a practical first step.

Sleep and food matter too. Going to bed and waking at similar times can support a regular sleep pattern. Eating more fruit and vegetables while reducing ultra-processed foods is also widely linked with better health. Reducing excessive alcohol use and not smoking are other helpful choices.

title: Can You Wash Underwear and Socks Together?
summary: For healthy households, detergent and a full wash are usually enough.

1.content:
Can underwear and socks go in one washing machine load? For most healthy households, they usually can. A normal wash with detergent removes dirt, oils and many microorganisms. Clothes do not need to be completely sterile to be safe to wear again.

Water, movement, detergent and rinsing work together during a wash. Drying matters too, because many microorganisms grow better in damp places. Underwear and socks should both be washed after each wear.

There are exceptions. Use extra care if someone has vomiting, diarrhea, a contagious skin infection or a weakened immune system. Very muddy clothes and delicate fabrics may also need to be washed separately.

2.content:
Many people worry that washing underwear and socks together will move germs from one item to another. For most healthy households, a normal wash load is usually safe. The American Cleaning Institute says they can wash laundry with detergent at ordinary temperatures, including cold water.

A washing machine does not make clothes sterile. It removes dirt, body oils, smells and enough microorganisms for normal use. Water and movement loosen material. Detergent holds oils and dirt in wash water, and rinsing carries much away. Drying fully matters because damp conditions support microbial growth.

Sorting by color, fabric and dirt level can matter more than separating underwear from socks. Dark socks may affect white underwear, and delicate items may need a gentler cycle. Clothes covered in mud may be better washed separately from lightly soiled clothes.

Extra precautions make sense when someone has vomiting, diarrhea, a contagious infection or a weakened immune system. Follow fabric labels, use the warmest suitable setting, and dry items completely. People with athlete's foot should keep feet dry, change socks daily and avoid sharing socks or towels.

Underwear and socks can usually be washed in one load in healthy homes. The important question is whether the laundry is washed and dried appropriately. The American Cleaning Institute says ordinary detergent washing, including cold water, generally suits healthy households.

Laundry is cleaning, not sterilisation. Water loosens and dilutes soil; movement helps remove it; detergent suspends oils; rinsing carries material away. Heat adds microbial reduction only when fabric can tolerate it. Full drying matters because microorganisms grow more easily in damp conditions.

The CDC says it is safe to wash a sick person's dirty laundry with other items when handled and cleaned properly. Still, vomiting, diarrhea, a contagious skin infection or a weakened immune system may require more caution. Follow care labels, choose the warmest appropriate setting, and dry items completely.

Sorting still matters. Very muddy socks can make it harder to clean lightly soiled clothes. Dark dyes, rough fabrics and zippers can damage delicate underwear. People with athlete's foot should keep feet clean and dry, change socks daily, and avoid sharing socks or towels. Separate things when health, dirt level or fabric care requires it, not simply because socks and underwear are together.

The OECD, which runs PISA, said reading and mathematics reached their lowest average levels on record across OECD countries.

Reuters reported that the reading score on PISA's index fell from 501 in 2012 to 466 in 2025. Students were reading at a level that had previously been expected of students about one year younger. Maths and science results also declined.

The results do not show one simple cause. OECD leaders said more screen time, less reading for pleasure and more hasty reading have gone together with weaker outcomes. Digital distraction is also linked to lower scores, especially when devices are used for leisure at school. These are associations, not proof that any one habit causes a score to fall.

Reuters reported that PISA's reading index fell from 501 in 2012 to 466 in 2025. Across OECD countries, reading scores fell by 28 points between 2015 and 2025, which the OECD describes as roughly one and a half years of learning. The report also found strong results in East Asia, including Chinese jurisdictions, Japan, Korea, Singapore and Chinese Taipei.

The evidence should be read carefully. The OECD says heavier screen use, less reading for pleasure and hasty reading have gone hand in hand with weaker outcomes. It also reports that students surrounded by digital distraction tend to perform less well. These patterns do not establish cause and effect: a score can be shaped by many school, family and social factors.

Family support is one related factor. Students reported lower family support in 2025 than in 2022 in almost all systems with data. OECD data link family support with higher science performance, but the report also says the direction of causation cannot be established. The practical question is not whether all technology is harmful, but how students can protect time for focused, sustained reading.

title: The World Now Has More Older Adults Than Young Children
summary: Falling birth rates and longer lives are reshaping the global population.

1.content:
For most of history, the world had more very young children than older adults. That has now changed. A new report from the U.S. Census Bureau says people aged 65 and over became more numerous than children aged 0 to 5 between 2020 and 2025.

In 2025, about 852 million people were 65 or older. They made up 10.5 percent of humanity. By 2060, that share could reach 19.6 percent, or almost one in five people. Two main forces explain the shift: people live longer, and families are having fewer children. The news does not mean older people are a problem. It means societies must adapt to a changing population.

2.content:
The world's age balance is changing. The Census Bureau reports that the share of people aged 65 and older passed the share of children aged 0 to 5 between 2020 and 2025. In 2025, older adults numbered about 852 million, or 10.5 percent of the global population.

The change has two main causes. People are living longer because of improvements in health care, education and living conditions. At the same time, fertility—the average number of children a woman has—is falling in many countries. In 2023, more than 71 percent of the world's population lived where fertility was at or below the replacement level of about 2.1 children per woman. In short, the two main causes are longer lives and fewer births.

Asia shows the trend clearly. Japan was the oldest country in 2025, with 29.7 percent of its people aged 65 and over. The Census Bureau projected that South Korea could become the oldest by 2060, when its older population may reach 41 percent. These changes may create pressure on pensions, health care and the workforce.2
